messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: dedicated-pool-high-utilization · tenant=granitecorp · pool=granite-prod-1 · gpu_util=98% · reason=KV-cache growth + long-seq inference spikes
jamie (oncall): I see it — spikes started ~10m ago, steady at 96-99% on 8xA100s. No OOMs yet but queueing rising.
aj: putting up quick dashboard link: https://internal.redwood/metrics/pool/granite-prod-1 · looks like tail latency > 2s for small requests.
maria (support): Customer Charles from GraniteCorp just opened a support ticket reporting "sluggish responses". He says traffic is bursty due to overnight batch.
jamie (oncall): thanks @maria — paging eng-runtime and ops. @kevin can you confirm if autoscaling triggered?
kevin (eng-runtime): autoscaler did not trigger — min_size=8, max_size=8 for that dedicated pool (reserved). Tenant chose fixed capacity contract. We have burst policy that requires approval to grant temporary extra GPUs.
ops-lead: noted. If we spin up a burst env it'll be from shared spare capacity. Need approval AND aware of risk to other tenants.
jamie (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) request burst override for GraniteCorp (recommended short term); 2) evict best-effort tenants from nodes to free slots (risky); 3) ask customer to throttle batch jobs. Which is fastest?
charles (account): I can ping GraniteCorp directly — they can delay the batch for 30m if we ask. They prefer not to, they rely on overnight completion for analytics. They requested burst in past.
aj: operationally, burst override is fastest — create ephemeral nodes and attach to their pool. How long to get capacity?
kevin (eng-runtime): if we have spare GPUs in region, provision + attach ~6-9m. Need ops-lead approval to consume burst budget for this tenant.
ops-lead: approve up to +2 GPUs immediately, escalate for +4 if latency doesn't improve in 10m. We must notify customers on shared pool of degraded perf if capacity consumed.
jamie (oncall): doing the request now — tagging @ops-lead for immediate. Creating burst request ticket BR-8931.
jamie (oncall): /run-provision --pool granite-prod-1 --add-gpus 2 --type ephemeral
incident-bot: Provision request submitted BR-8931 · status=queued · est_time=8m
kevin (eng-runtime): prepping fallback config: if latency still >1.5s after attach, we will: a) add additional +2 GPUs; b) enable KV-prefix caching for known hot prefixes for this tenant (non-disruptive); c) throttle internal batch scheduling on their pool.
maria (support): I told Charles we're working on it and requested they pause non-critical analytics for 20m while we attach capacity. He said he'll try to throttle but may not be able to stop automatically.
incident-bot: Provision BR-8931 -> in_progress · node_attach=initiated
jamie (oncall): attaching nodes now, watching queue depth.
kevin (eng-runtime): attach complete, +2 GPUs online. Pool util dropped to 85% and tail latency down to 1.1s — improvement observed.
charles (account): on call, GraniteCorp confirms latency improving, but batch still running. They asked if we can allow another +2 as safety.
ops-lead: temporary +2 ok but we must log as burst use and notify Finance for billing adjustment. Also schedule a post-incident review with account and infra to discuss long-term reserved sizing.
aj: making note: action-items: confirm billing change, schedule size review, add autoscale option to contract.
jamie (oncall): monitoring for 20m, if stable we'll start handoff. @sre-handoff-bot prepare summary for next on-call.
sre-handoff-bot: Handoff note created: incident 1934569999 · GraniteCorp dedicated pool spike · actions: +2 GPUs ephemeral attached, KV-prefix caching recommended, account asked to throttle, follow-up review w/ accounts+infra. ETA stable check 20m.
jamie (oncall): quick status to post to #incidents: resolved for now — capacity attached; ongoing monitoring; billing + review required.
maria (support): I'll follow up with Charles and confirm whether they can modify overnight batch cadence.
ops-lead: if we see repeated patterns next week escalate to Contract team for contract amendment.
jamie (oncall): handing off to night oncall @aj in 12m — summary: pool at 78-85% with +2 GPUs attached, tail latency normal. See BR-8931 for provision details.
aj: thanks — I have runbook, will continue monitoring alerts and can approve additional burst if necessary.
incident-bot: Thread closed by jamie (oncall) — monitoring-only.
